name: Okinawa · Naha
tagline: Ryukyu castles, coral seas and island food
summary: Okinawa was the independent Ryukyu Kingdom until 1879, and its culture still feels different from mainland Japan. Naha has the rebuilt Shuri Castle and the lively Kokusai-dōri, while the island has turquoise beaches, one of the world's largest aquariums and somber Second World War memorials.
seasonNote: March, April, October and November are warm and less humid. The rainy season runs from May to June; July to September is hot, with typhoons. Winter is mild but too cool for swimming.
arrival: Fly to Naha Airport from Tokyo (about 2.5 hours), Osaka, Fukuoka, Seoul or Taipei. The Yui Rail monorail runs to the city centre.
gettingAround: The monorail covers Naha; rent a car for the rest of the island, as buses are slow.
cashTip: Cards are increasingly accepted, but carry yen for small restaurants and markets.
foodTip: Okinawa soba, goya champuru, taco rice, sea grapes and Orion beer.
buyTip: Ryukyu glass, Tsuboya pottery, shisa lion figures and brown sugar sweets.
